hypotheses.claim: Crash rate is proportional to how often humans make mistakes (elasticity 1)
hypotheses.prediction: b = 1 in log(crash rate) = a + b log(mistake multiplier)
hypotheses.test: Poisson regression over 1x-30x, Wald test of b = 1
hypotheses.follow_up: attribute crashes to mechanisms (Shapley over the Behaviour knobs): which mistakes actually make crashes?

hypotheses.claim: Denser traffic is more dangerous per vehicle-hour
hypotheses.prediction: b > 0 in log(crash rate) = a + b log(demand), demand 0.5x-2x
hypotheses.effect: b = -0.39 [-0.79, 0.01] per vehicle-hour; per vehicle-km b = 0.07 [-0.34, 0.47]
hypotheses.follow_up: exposure matters: report every crash rate per hour, per km and per junction entry, and show where they disagree

hypotheses.claim: Wet roads (friction 0.6) raise the crash rate by at least 50 %
hypotheses.test: exact conditional rate ratio; one-sided test of RR >= 1.5
hypotheses.follow_up: a friction dose-response (1.0 .. 0.3) with 4x the copies: where does the cliff between wet and icy start?

hypotheses.claim: Crashes fall in a straight line as the AV share grows
hypotheses.prediction: no curvature: the quadratic term adds nothing (log-linear model fits)
hypotheses.test: LRT of a quadratic term in a Poisson regression on 0-100 % AVs
hypotheses.follow_up: the AV-share curve with 9 shares and 3x the copies: is there a threshold (convexity) or diminishing returns?

hypotheses.claim: Doing well on everyday traffic and on long-tail incidents is the same skill
hypotheses.prediction: Spearman rho >= 0.8 between core and long-tail scores (15 drivers)
hypotheses.test: Spearman, permutation p, bootstrap CI; refuted if CI excludes 0.8
hypotheses.follow_up: a 3-scenario 'core' subset that predicts the full 18-scenario score: a cheaper benchmark

hypotheses.claim: A driver that passes more absolute safety checks gets a higher overall score
hypotheses.prediction: rho > 0 and the top scorer passes the most checks
hypotheses.effect: rho = 0.82 [0.45, 0.96]; the top scorer (rule-based AV, 77.2) passes 104 checks, the most passed is 123
hypotheses.follow_up: a Pareto view of score vs checks: what the rule-based AV does that learned policies do not (comfort, speed)

hypotheses.claim: Retraining the same RL recipe reproduces its score within 5 points
hypotheses.prediction: |score(retrain) - score(original)| <= 5 per scenario, on average and typically
hypotheses.effect: mean diff -3.4 [-13.1, +6.2]; per-scenario sd 36.3; core means -7.2, -1.6, -10.2
hypotheses.follow_up: seed variance of RL on AVBench: 10 seeds per recipe on a GPU, with confidence intervals on every leaderboard row

hypotheses.claim: Policies trained in Oakland transfer to other neighbourhoods unchanged
hypotheses.test: Wilcoxon signed-rank over 15 drivers, bootstrap CI of the mean
hypotheses.follow_up: train on a mix of Oakland, Squirrel Hill and Downtown: does the transfer gap close, and at what cost at home?

hypotheses.claim: Faster AVs crash more: there is a speed-safety trade-off
hypotheses.prediction: rho > 0 between progress and unaided crash rate (driver x scenario)
hypotheses.follow_up: the speed-safety frontier: a policy family indexed by one speed knob, with the frontier's slope and its kinks

hypotheses.claim: How often the safety filter steps in predicts how unsafe the policy is without it
hypotheses.prediction: rho > 0.5 between filter share and unaided crash rate
hypotheses.follow_up: filter dependence as a deployment metric: when does a filtered policy's record overstate its own safety?

hypotheses.claim: Fog hurts the detection of pedestrians and cyclists more than of vehicles
hypotheses.prediction: relative drop in detection rate (fog 0.7 vs clear) larger for VRUs
hypotheses.test: sensor model on 12 AVs' trips, cluster bootstrap over AVs
hypotheses.effect: relative drop VRU 38% vs vehicles 35%; difference +3% [-3%, +8%] (2858 VRU object-frames)
hypotheses.follow_up: per-class sensor curves under fog, rain and night, with 10x the egos to resolve a few-point difference
